name: issue_821_comfort_floor_fallback_no_confidence
description: Reproduces the reported live incident (Zone "Simulated 2"): a day classified for cooling, no nat-vent session, indoor decays below comfort_heat with NO thermal-model confidence (confidence_k_passive == "none" — the exact condition Zone 2 had during the incident window). The ODE floor guard cannot help here (MODEL_INELIGIBLE) — this scenario proves the confidence-none FALLBACK path is what actually fixes the reported bug: a simple, sustain-confirmed indoor-vs-comfort_heat check that switches the comfort family to heating.
source: Issue #821 investigation — live incident, Zone "Simulated 2" (climate.simulated_thermostat), indoor held at 57F for 2+ hours while CA repeatedly confirmed a 74F cool setpoint every cycle with zero corrective heating.
notes: (a) Scenario effectiveness: reverting Issue #821's fallback path (removing the confidence-none branch from _resolve_comfort_family_mode(), or removing its wiring into _apply_comfort_band()) causes the final assertion (comfort_family=heating at 08:41) to FAIL — the engine would keep affirming the cool-mode ceiling forever, exactly reproducing the reported incident.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md's automation logic table now documents the comfort-floor-defense fallback row alongside this scenario as its test reference.

(c) Occupant experience: without this fix, a zone with no thermal-model history yet (a freshly-added zone, or one that hasn't accumulated enough HVAC cycles) never gets its comfort floor actively defended on a cool-classified day — the home can drift arbitrarily cold with the thermostat still confirming a cooling setpoint every cycle. With the fix, the engine switches to heat once the below-floor reading has genuinely held for COMFORT_FALLBACK_CONFIRM_S (90s), not on a single noisy tick.

The 08:30:00 assertion (family still 'cooling') proves the sustain-confirmation gate is genuinely load-bearing here — the first evaluation after crossing below the floor does NOT escalate immediately, matching the project owner's explicit concern about avoiding a naive instant-flip design.

CORRECTED per Issue #823 (this scenario's own commentary previously endorsed the bug it should have caught): _arm_comfort_family() must NOT reset the family-switch lockout's dwell clock on every routine reassertion of an unchanged family (_apply_comfort_band()/_set_temperature_for_mode() now pass only_if_changed=True). The dwell clock measures continuous time since the 'cooling' family GENUINELY started (08:00:00, the scenario's baseline classification tick, the first real arm), not time since the most recent reassertion. The added 08:35:00 classification tick (below the floor, day still cool-classified, matching the ~5-minute cadence observed in the live incident) exists specifically to distinguish the fixed behavior from the pre-#823 bug: under the bug, that tick would reset entry_time to 08:35:00, leaving only 360s of headroom by 08:41:00 (< 600s comfort_mode_switch_min_interval_s) — the final assertion would FAIL, reproducing the live incident. Under the fix, entry_time stays pinned at 08:00:00 through every reassertion (08:30:00, 08:35:00), so by 08:41:00 elapsed is ~2460s, and the only real gate remaining is COMFORT_FALLBACK_CONFIRM_S (90s) from the 08:30:00 below-floor crossing — comfortably satisfied.

Negative-control equivalent for this scenario lives in tests/test_comfort_mode_family_lockout.py::TestPermanentLockoutFixIssue823 (unit-level, exercises 15 closely-spaced cycles rather than this scenario's 2) — that test's own negative control (reverting only_if_changed to a no-op) was manually confirmed to fail, i.e. the lockout never clears. This JSON scenario is the end-to-end/production-shaped counterpart, not a duplicate: it exercises the real event/classification harness path, not just the two engine methods directly.

events.note: Warm-day classification: HVAC in cool mode. No nat-vent (fan_mode disabled) — mirrors the reported Zone 2 incident, a dev-sim zone with no WHF configured.
Baseline: indoor 71F within band [70F, 74F] — comfort band arms normally at the ceiling (cool).

Indoor has decayed to 67F, below comfort_heat=70F — no thermal model has ever been set on this engine, so confidence_k_passive defaults to "none" (the exact confidence-none condition Zone 2 had during the real incident).

Re-evaluation with indoor now below the floor. First tick the fallback candidate becomes true — armed, not yet confirmed (elapsed 0s < 90s COMFORT_FALLBACK_CONFIRM_S), so the band still commands cool this cycle. Per the Issue #823 fix, this reassertion does NOT reset the family-switch lockout's entry_time (only_if_changed=True) — it stays pinned at 08:00:00, when 'cooling' genuinely became the active family.

Issue #823: a third, realistically-spaced re-evaluation (5 minutes after 08:30:00, matching the live incident's observed classification cadence) — indoor is still below the floor, and the fallback candidate is already sustain-confirmed (300s elapsed since the 08:30:00 crossing, past the 90s COMFORT_FALLBACK_CONFIRM_S gate). This is the tick that discriminates the Issue #823 fix from the bug it replaces. Under the FIX, entry_time has stayed pinned at 08:00:00 (the true start of the 'cooling' family) since the 08:30:00 reassertion was a no-op — elapsed is already ~2100s, past the 600s lockout, so the switch to heating actually fires HERE, at 08:35:00, not at the final 08:41:00 checkpoint. Under the pre-fix BUG, the 08:30:00 reassertion would have reset entry_time to 08:30:00, so at 08:35:00 elapsed is only 300s (< 600s) — still locked out; this tick's own reassertion then resets entry_time again to 08:35:00, so by 08:41:00 elapsed is only 360s (< 600s) — still locked out, reproducing the live incident's permanent lockout. Either way, the scenario's only assertion type here reads the engine's FINAL state (see the 08:41:00 assertion's own note), so this tick's effect is only visible indirectly via whether the final snapshot shows 'heating' or 'cooling'.

Final re-evaluation. Elapsed since the TRUE cooling-family start (08:00:00) is ~2460s, comfortably past comfort_mode_switch_min_interval_s (600s); COMFORT_FALLBACK_CONFIRM_S (90s from the 08:30:00 below-floor crossing) was already satisfied by 08:35:00. Fallback escalates: comfort family switches to heating, engine commands heat at comfort_heat.

assertions.reason: Baseline: warm day, indoor within band — comfort band arms normally (proves the scenario's own baseline setup is sound before the below-floor decay).

By 08:41:00, elapsed since the TRUE cooling-family start (08:00:00, per the Issue #823 fix — routine reassertions at 08:30:00 and 08:35:00 are no-ops for the dwell clock) is ~2460s, comfortably past comfort_mode_switch_min_interval_s (600s), and COMFORT_FALLBACK_CONFIRM_S (90s from the 08:30:00 below-floor crossing) was satisfied by 08:31:30. In practice the fallback actually escalates at the 08:35:00 tick (the first re-evaluation after both gates clear) and 'heating' is already the recorded family by the time this assertion checks — this checkpoint just confirms it holds. This is the actual fix for the reported live incident (Zone "Simulated 2", confidence_k_passive == "none" throughout the 2+ hour incident window). NOTE: the 'comfort_family' assertion type reads the engine's FINAL state snapshot (matching the existing nat_vent_still_active/paused_by_door convention documented in outcomes.py) — it cannot verify an intermediate mid-run value, only the state at scenario end, which is why this is the only assertion of this type in the scenario and is placed on the LAST event.

verdict.summary: On a cool-classified day with no thermal-model confidence, the comfort floor is actively defended via the sustain-confirmed fallback path once indoor genuinely holds below comfort_heat for 90s.
verdict.observed_behavior: comfort family stays 'cooling' on the tick indoor first crosses below comfort_heat, then switches to 'heating' once the below-floor reading has been sustained for COMFORT_FALLBACK_CONFIRM_S.
verdict.expected_behavior: The comfort floor is never silently left undefended on a cool-classified day, and the switch is debounced against a single noisy reading — directly fixing the reported live incident without reintroducing heat/cool hunting.
